setup: Sit on the floor or on a firm chair with an upright posture.
Extend one leg straight out in front of you with the heel resting on the ground.
Optionally loop a strap, towel, or your hands around the ball of the extended foot.
steps: Gently pull the toes and the ball of the foot back toward your shin until you feel a comfortable stretch along the back of the lower leg.
Maintain a tall torso and keep the knee straight without hyperextending it.
Hold the stretch steadily for the desired duration.
Release the tension slowly, then switch to the opposite leg.
instructions.breathing: Breathe smoothly and deeply, exhaling as you gently deepen the stretch.

common_faults.fault: Slouching through the spine to reach the toes.
common_faults.correction: Sit tall from the hips and use a strap or towel if you cannot comfortably reach the foot.

common_faults.fault: Aggressively forcing the foot into extreme dorsiflexion.
common_faults.correction: Apply gentle, progressive tension to produce a mild stretch rather than sharp pain.

precautions: Avoid forceful bouncing or aggressive pulling, especially if rehabilitating an Achilles tendon or calf injury.

name: Seated Calf Stretch
summary: A seated flexibility exercise that stretches the calf muscles by pulling the foot and toes into dorsiflexion.
